title: Leverage and systems
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you have that another company wants, without it costing them anything?

A student said that when they had very limited resources, the people in the book got creative. One example was a deal with a company that held a map database: they licensed it for free until they started making a profit. It let them start building without capital.

I said: which is a great lesson, leverage number one. People don't understand the resources they have, and having a strategy and going to a company with a way for them to grow through what you are doing. It's differentiating yourself.

You open a market for another company that they didn't see. There is no loss for them, no risk, only upside, I said. It gives you an amazing amount of leverage. A student said: super hard to say no to.
People can get greedy and stupid, I said. We go with the intellect first, and we don't let ego get in the way of the growth of a company.

My own example: with a landscape company doing a million a year, I ask: would you be interested in adding another million to your bottom line per year? I'm not going to change what you are already doing. And I've got a manual of operations that will help in your own business as well.

I had capitalized on an asset I didn't have: a company with eight thousand clients who have lakes and ponds. The next challenge is operations, I said: getting people to do something they have never done before.

groups.heading: What do you put in place?

lines.text: A student said: motivation and education. I said: think about changing the behaviour of people who have done the same thing for thirty-five years. Sometimes you have to bring in a new operator.

What do you put in place to change it? the student said: the system. I said: yes, it's the operation manual, the standard operating procedures and the metrics. The person in the book is learning to put those systems in place right now, at an early age.
What can you offer someone with no risk to them, and what system would make it run?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you have that you may not see as a resource.
Write a company that could grow through what you do.
Write the offer with no downside and no risk for them.
Write what you are asking them to do that they have never done before.
Write the system you would put in place: manual, procedures, metrics.

check.q: What did I call the lesson from the free map-database deal?
What did I say makes an offer hard to refuse?
choices: No loss, no risk, only upside

check.q: What did I say you put in place to change an organization?
choices: The system: manual, procedures and metrics

recap: Offer upside with no risk. Put the system in place that makes it run.
